findings.detail: The stem of M4-S32-T1 shows the correct loop: after each stop_reason "tool_use" response, the loop executed the tool, returned its result and continued. M4-S39-T2 asks what to do when code treats a "tool_use" response as final. Its answer, D (return the result and keep looping while stop_reason is "tool_use"), can be read directly off M4-S32-T1. In the other direction, M4-S39-T2 option D hints that the loop stops once stop_reason is no longer "tool_use", which is the answer of M4-S32-T1.

The correct option A of M4-S45-T1 says to split a multi-concern customer message into distinct items, investigate each one and synthesize one resolution. This gives away the answer of M4-S43-T1, option C: list every issue in the multi-issue request and delegate one subtask for each. Both questions also share a nearly identical wrong option B (escalate multi-issue messages), which makes the link easy to see.
